criteria.label: CLOSE
similar: Both use blackened metal, beveled industrial frames, and worn surface texture.
Both pair amber accents with cyan highlights over charcoal map imagery.
Both include embossed or patterned metal detailing.
different: REFERENCE is warmer and more uniformly burnished; CANDIDATE has brighter silver edging and flatter black interiors.
CANDIDATE varies more in texture and asset-detail scale across cards.

evidence.observation: Warm, dark patterned metal with bronze bevels and restrained cyan/amber accents.
Closely matching industrial metal treatment, but with shinier silver borders.
Route panel maintains layered, textured metal and warm inset framing.

criteria.label: RELATED
similar: Both use compact top resource bars, centered inspectors, and vertical build palettes.
Both integrate dark industrial overlays directly over the isometric map.
Amber denotes planning or warnings while cyan marks active selections.
different: REFERENCE inspectors use larger assets, stronger metric hierarchy, and denser framed rows.
CANDIDATE route cards have flatter black interiors, smaller copy, and substantially more empty space.
CANDIDATE shows more clipping and inconsistent icon scale in the inspector and tool palette.

evidence.observation: Large substation image, prominent capacity metric, segmented meter, and clear framed hierarchy.
Same inspector role, but the asset is much smaller and the heading is visibly clipped.
Dense comparison card uses icons, aligned metrics, and nested borders.

criteria.label: CLOSE
similar: Both are independent centered bottom strips with four contiguous beveled cells.
Both use dark industrial chrome, muted inactive states, and cyan active-state emphasis.
Their overall footprint and separation from the map are closely matched.
different: CANDIDATE is slightly wider and packs progress text plus status icons into the cells.
REFERENCE uses larger simple symbols and speed values with more breathing room.

evidence.observation: Centered four-cell strip with a cyan second cell and clearly separated playback states.
Centered four-stage event bar with visible progress, active stage, result, and next states.
